subject: Dedicated capacity pricing — reserve GPU sizing & token economics
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Moore <alyssa@medlytics.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing — reserve GPU sizing & token economics

Hi Alyssa — great conversation today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and a small set of asks so we can turn the call into a clear proposal: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Two primary workloads: (1) patient-facing summarization microservice (~low latency, 1–2s target) and (2) back-office clinical QA batch jobs (higher throughput, more tolerant latency).
- Expected steady-state monthly consumption: roughly 150M–300M tokens/month (you mentioned 4–10M/day as a window) — with spikes up to ~20M tokens/day during pilot.
- Preferred GPU family: you flagged H100s for 2–3x perf on long-context generative workloads, but also open to A100 if cost is the priority.
- Target unit economics: you asked us to show options that hit ~$15–$25 per 1M tokens (target ~$20/1M tokens).
- Procurement: Medlytics procurement will require an MSA + SOW and PO process.

Key clarifying questions (we need answers to finalize pricing bands)
1) Can you confirm the 150M–300M tokens/month range as the best estimate for the next 6 months? If not, please provide a conservative and upside number.
2) For the patient-facing service: target p95 latency SLO and target concurrency (requests/sec) — we want to size KV cache and batching correctly.
3) Preferred GPU: do you want a pricing comparison (A100 vs H100) at the committed-band level, or should we only price the H100 path?

What we’ll deliver after clarification
- A committed-capacity proposal mapping 3 reserve bands (small/medium/large) to GPUs, throughput (tokens/sec), and a per-1M-token unit price. See attached MAPS_token_estimate.xlsx for a worked example.
- Draft commercial terms (MSA + 30-day SOW) and an initial estimate of SLA/credits.

Action items and owners
- Alyssa: confirm monthly range + p95 latency target by EOD Mon (Jan 19).
- Soojin: prepare 3-band reserve pricing and TCO model (deliver by Wed Jan 21).
- Dylan: validate region capacity for H100 availability (internal).
- Neha: run a quick sensitivity for $/1M tokens at 150M/250M/350M monthly tokens.

Attachments: MAPS_token_estimate.xlsx (worked token-to-GPU mapping), Redwood-dedicated-pricing-playbook.pdf (approach), procurement-MSA-draft.docx (template).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m follow-up if it helps.

Best,
Soojin Lee

From: Alyssa Moore <alyssa@medlytics.ai>

Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing — reserve GPU sizing & token economics

Soojin — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments (downloading now). Quick answers inline: 

1) Monthly range: our conservative plan is 120M tokens/month, expected cadence ~220M/month, upside (scale) 420M/month over 6 months if pilot goes well. The internal forecast is attached (Medlytics-usage-forecast.csv).
2) Patient-facing SLO: p95 <= 1.5s, typical concurrency target is 40 concurrent requests with short contexts (~1k tokens/request average). Back-office batch job runs overnight and needs sustained throughput ~300k tokens/sec for windows of 30–60 minutes.
3) GPU family: procurement prefers A100 for cost reasons, but Engineering prefers H100 for the patient-facing models. We need pricing that shows both — can you give committed-band pricing for both A100 and H100?

Procurement note: we will require a 60-day review period for the MSA and standard PO flow. I’ll loop in our legal if we get to final commercial terms.

If you can get the three-band proposal showing committed monthly tokens, corresponding reserved GPU count (A100/H100 options), and the implied $/1M token price, we can review and pick a band.

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Moore
Head of Platform Integrations | Medlytics
alyssa@medlytics.ai | +1 212-555-0199

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Moore <alyssa@medlytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing — reserve GPU sizing & token economics

Alyssa — perfect, thanks for the forecast and the SLO targets. We’ll do the A100/H100 comparison across three reserved bands. High-level preview below so you have context before the formal spreadsheet: 

Preview (illustrative numbers, final model attached Wed)
- Small band (entry): 4x A100 or 2x H100 equivalent — steady tokens/month ~100M–200M; implied price ~ $28/1M (A100) or $22/1M (H100) with 12-month reservation.
- Medium band (recommended pilot): 8x A100 or 4x H100 — steady tokens/month ~200M–400M; implied price ~ $20/1M (A100) or $16/1M (H100).
- Large band (enterprise): 16x A100 or 8x H100 — steady tokens/month >400M; implied price ~ $14/1M (A100) or $11/1M (H100).

Notes:
- These are unit-level token economics that include baseline model costs, GPU amortization, and average batching/caching assumptions for your 1k-token request profile. They assume a 12-month reserved commitment. We’ll show sensitivity to 6/12/24 month terms in the model.
- For the patient-facing SLO (p95 <= 1.5s) we recommend the medium H100 band to hit headroom for concurrency + KV cache. If you want cost-first, the medium A100 band is the cheaper upfront option.

Next internal steps: Ben  can you validate whether we can guarantee H100 availability in us-west2 for a 4x H100 reserve? Dylan, please also confirm ops availability and any lead time.

I’ll push the full three-band workbook (A100 & H100 columns, tokens->throughput mapping, and draft commercial terms) by Wed Jan 21. After that we can schedule a 30m decision call.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
